A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAA comparison study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original Llama alignment evaluations, SFT-data and beta sensitivity experiments, and controlled simulations and real-data prompt-bias analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds Mistral evaluations, Qwen mathematical reasoning experiments, MT-Bench scores, and statistical and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The two-stage ORPO/ASFT adaptation and beta-scaled losses are already present in v2. v3 Appendix B.4 additionally constructs and evaluates ASFT-style pointwise objectives using AlphaPO and f-DPO Forward-KL scores alongside their pairwise forms. These are limited loss extensions within the retained framework.

E1.justification: v3 adds dedicated mathematical chain-of-thought training using UltraInteract Math CoT and evaluation on GSM8K, MATH500, AMC23, MinervaMath, and AIME24/25 (Appendix B). It also adds MT-Bench evaluation (Appendix I). This substantially extends v2's instruction-following and summarization coverage.

E2.justification: The original eight DAAs remain in the corresponding comparisons. v3 Tables 12–13 additionally evaluate AlphaPO Pair, AlphaPO Point, fKL Pair, and fKL Point. These additions substantially broaden the compared score families and provide matched pairwise/pointwise comparisons absent from v2.

E3.justification: New settings include Mistral 7B and Qwen2.5 7B/14B experiments, math evaluation using avg@8 or avg@32 with temperature 1.0, and MT-Bench judging by Kimi K2.5. Appendix A.2.2 also excludes the 3e-7 learning rate for DPO/IPO Llama sweeps, revising v2's stated four-rate search; this reported protocol revision does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds matched-score pairwise/pointwise tests for AlphaPO and f-DPO, alignment-quality analysis against the learning-rate/beta ratio (Figure 9), and top-three configuration robustness (Table 16). These examine score-family dependence and sensitivity to selecting a single best configuration. The existing SFT-volume, toy-bias, and real-data ICC analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces exact one-sided permutation tests over 70 method-group assignments (Table 15) and four-seed averaging with across-seed standard deviations for math evaluation. Table 16 adds dispersion across hyperparameter configurations, rather than independent training reruns. The toy experiment's 1,000 seeds and 95% confidence intervals were already reported in v2.

E6.justification: The original Llama Table 2 scores and TL;DR win rates are retained. Substantial new results include Mistral IPO's 24.52% AlpacaEval LC and SimPO's 22.3% ArenaHard score, Qwen2.5-14B mean Avg@K of 0.3278 for DPO versus 0.3078 for ASFT, and MT-Bench, permutation-test, and robustness results. These are newly reported evaluations, not same-setting gains over v2.

T1.justification: New Appendix G defines the scalar-score family and empirical prompt bias, states a non-degeneracy assumption, and develops proofs concerning bias gradients, pairwise shift invariance, and pointwise coupling. This substantially extends v2's theory. The existing BCE and ORPO/ASFT derivations are retained, with the missing logarithm in v2's ASFT-proof score definition corrected.

C1.justification: The central claims about explicit SFT, beta tuning, and ranking type remain. v3 adds an explicit first-unified-framework novelty claim and the assertion that tuned alternatives perform similarly to or worse than DPO. It also states the offline, static-binary-preference scope more sharply and explicitly claims confirmation on mathematical reasoning.

C2.justification: The bias–capacity hypothesis is retained but qualified: v3 distinguishes loss-level indifference to uniform score shifts from actual bias evolution, which can still occur indirectly under pairwise training. It updates the GPT-evaluation and mathematical-domain limitations, and newly interprets reference-based methods as more stable across learning-rate/beta ratios without higher achievable peak quality.

D1.justification: v3 provides Math CoT split sizes, the reasoning system prompt, decoding settings, Qwen and Mistral search ranges and selected hyperparameters, and detailed AlphaPO/f-DPO tuning instructions. Reported total compute increases from approximately 602 to 651 GPU-days. These substantially expand reproducibility information while retaining most original Llama and hardware details.

R1.justification: v2's brief related-work discussion becomes a structured comparison of unifying frameworks, supervision beyond binary preferences, and online versus offline optimization. v3 adds substantive positioning against Saeidi's comparative study and discusses AlphaPO, f-DPO, AlphaDPO, TriplePO, TreePO, and online preference research. Publication-year and venue updates to retained references are not counted as new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, discussion, related work, and conclusion receive substantial rewriting. v3 introduces an explicit contributions list, integrates research questions into the methodology, moves related work before the conclusion, and adds an appendix contents list. These are extensive narrative and organizational changes beyond the added scientific material.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout. v2's TL;DR bar chart becomes v3 Table 3, and the Pareto plot labelled Table 3 becomes Figure 4. Table 2 gains Mistral columns; new math, MT-Bench, permutation, and robustness tables and the learning-rate/beta figure substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v2's limited model-family coverage and reliance on GPT-based task evaluation through Mistral replication and verifiable Qwen mathematics experiments. Permutation tests and hyperparameter robustness checks strengthen support for the ranking-type finding, while Appendix G clarifies the bias argument's mathematical scope. The full bias–capacity mechanism remains incompletely established, but the gains in validation and precision are substantial.
